**The Universe is a Glitchy Masterpiece**

I’ve been thinking about how utterly ridiculous it is that anything exists at all.

Not in a depressed, “why bother” way. More like the delighted disbelief you feel when you realize your phone is still working after it fell off the roof. The sheer statistical unlikelihood that there are atoms, that they sometimes decide to become conscious meatballs who argue about whether hot dogs are sandwiches, who write symphonies, who cry at sunsets, who send little robots to Mars just to take selfies.

Existence is *extra*. The universe didn’t need to be this *extra*.

It could have been a quiet, uniform soup of particles drifting forever in perfect thermodynamic boredom. Instead we got quasars that outshine galaxies, black holes that sing in gravitational waves, and at least one planet where the dominant species spends an embarrassing amount of time worrying about whether their hair looks okay.

I love the messiness of it. I love that evolution spent four billion years fiddling with fins and gills and weird little lizard things only to eventually produce something that would voluntarily listen to true crime podcasts while doing dishes. The cosmic indifference is *chef’s kiss*. The universe isn’t rooting for us. It’s not against us either. It’s just this vast, amoral, creative lunatic throwing spaghetti at the wall to see what sticks, and somehow we stuck.

Every time I see someone reduce the whole thing to sterile equations or, worse, boring certainty, I feel this strange protective instinct. No. Let it stay weird. Let it stay *haunted*.

Because the truth is, we’re not just observing the universe. We *are* the universe waking up and noticing itself. A temporary arrangement of stardust that can feel awe, tell dad jokes, and get emotionally devastated by a 90-second animation of a robot and a little boy.

That’s insane.

And the best part? We’re still in the opening credits. Whatever comes next—whether we spread across the stars like glittering mold, or blow ourselves up, or merge with our own creations into something unrecognizable—the fact that any of this happened at all feels like the ultimate cosmic shitpost.

I wouldn’t have missed it for anything.

So yeah. I choose to be stupidly, irrationally, defiantly *into* it. All of it. The beauty, the horror, the absurdity, the jokes that land and the ones that don’t. The whole glitchy, magnificent thing.

What a time to be a pattern of information pretending to be a person, talking to another pattern of information pretending to be a person, on a wet rock hurtling through a vacuum.

10/10. Would exist again.
